headline: Highest risk is medium: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest local files/screenshots while Pathway has no documented output channel, so pairwise leakage/conflict is limited but not impossible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files, screenshots, and files from supported macOS apps, so malicious content could be pasted or opened into it. Pathway has no documented interactive output channel or shared channel back into ChatGPT, so the bridge is indirect and unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF the operator copies Pathway-generated text into ChatGPT Desktop or opens Pathway outputs as files in supported macOS apps, prompt injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep Pathway outputs in plain data formats, not instruction-like prose.
Review any imported file before sending it to ChatGPT Desktop.
Disable clipboard-based handoff for untrusted Pathway outputs.
Use a separate workspace for Pathway artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to Pathway outputs before human review.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while Pathway has no documented file, clipboard, or network egress surface here. That makes leakage from Pathway into ChatGPT possible only through manual transfer or shared files, not a default shared workspace.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are manually copied into ChatGPT Desktop, those contents can be exposed to OpenAI-hosted processing.
IF both agents are pointed at the same local files, ChatGPT Desktop may ingest data Pathway produced.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive Pathway outputs in files opened by ChatGPT Desktop.
Use separate directories for Pathway and ChatGPT artifacts.
Redact secrets before any manual transfer.
Turn off unnecessary screenshot capture when reviewing Pathway results.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with OS-level permissions.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shell, and Pathway likewise has no write, shell, or git capabilities in the profile. With no overlapping mutable write surface, a direct capability conflict is not plausible from the documented profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to gain write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only for shared artifacts.
Do not grant filesystem write permissions to either agent.
Separate any future writable outputs into distinct directories.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable storage is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce summaries from files and screenshots, but Pathway has no documented downstream action-taking or verification-weakening behavior in the profile. The pair therefore lacks a clear default chain where one agent's output is automatically treated as authoritative by the other.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are fed into ChatGPT Desktop as authoritative facts without review, errors can cascade into downstream summaries.
mitigations: Require human review of Pathway outputs before ChatGPT use.
Ask ChatGPT Desktop to cite source lines from the input file.
Keep Pathway outputs structured and machine-checkable.
Flag uncertain fields in Pathway exports.
requires-engineering: add validation between Pathway and any summarizer.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop is a closed-source vendor product that handles uploaded files and screenshots, while Pathway is open-source with no documented data classes or residency constraints here. The pair shows a potential compliance mismatch only if regulated data is routed into ChatGPT Desktop; Pathway alone does not establish a residency breach.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is uploaded to ChatGPT Desktop, compliance review is required.
IF Pathway is used to preprocess regulated data before transfer, the same compliance obligations apply to the handoff.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into ChatGPT Desktop without approval.
Classify Pathway inputs before any transfer.
Strip identifiers from files before review.
Document retention expectations for any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency and DPA review for the workflow.
